body:
Assume the basket of goods and services bought by level 100 Economics students in UCC is transport, clothes, power, movie shows, diet drinks and popcorn. The cost of these items in the basket in 2005 was GH₵50, GH₵30, GH₵20, GH₵5, GH₵0.70 and GH₵1.00 respectively. Quantities purchased during this period were one, five, ten, three, three hundred and five hundred respectively. The table below provides **percentage changes** in both prices and quantities.

| Item | 2006 P | 2006 Q | 2007 P | 2007 Q | 2008 P | 2008 Q | 2009 P | 2009 Q | 2010 P | 2010 Q |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transport | 60 | 10 | 25 | 5 | 20 | 6 | 10 | 7 | 15 | 8 |
| Clothes | 67 | 1 | 20 | 3 | 15 | 0 | −5 | 20 | 10 | 2 |
| Power | 50 | 2 | 30 | 4 | 20 | −2 | 10 | −1 | 0 | 20 |
| Movie shows | 50 | 0 | 5 | 5 | 20 | −2 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 21 |
| Diet drinks | 13 | 0 | −6 | 20 | 2 | 2 | −2 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| Popcorn | 0 | 20 | 5 | 5 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 2 |

(a) Compute the consumer price index using 2005 as the base year.
(b) What was the rate of inflation for all the years, using the CPI you calculated in (a)?
(c) Now compute the CPI for each of the years, using 2008 as the base year instead of 2005 but using the same "market bundle."
(d) What was the rate of inflation from 2008 to 2010, using the CPI you calculated in (c)? Is it the same as your answer to (b)?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A Laspeyres CPI uses fixed base-period quantities: $CPI_t = \sum p_t q_0 / \sum p_0 q_0 \times 100$. Rebasing divides every index by the new base-year value, which leaves ratios between years (and hence inflation rates) unchanged. The quantity percentages are a distractor for a fixed-basket index.

## Simplified explanation

Work out each year's prices from the percentage changes, price the same 2005 shopping basket each year and compare with 2005. Changing the base year changes the numbers but not the inflation rate.
hint: Hold the 2005 basket fixed and compound the price changes.

body:
In a fractional reserve banking system, the money supply is influenced by the behaviour of the public and commercial banks, as well as the policies of the central bank. Assume the following parameters:

Required reserve ratio = 10%; currency-to-deposit ratio = 0.2; excess reserve ratio = 0.05; monetary base = GHS 5,000.

(a) Derive the formula for the money multiplier using the concepts of the currency-to-deposit ratio, required reserve ratio and excess reserve ratio. Clearly explain the economic meaning of each component. **(4 marks)**
(b) Using the values provided, calculate the money multiplier. **(4 marks)**
(c) Based on your result in (b), compute the total money supply in the economy. **(4 marks)**
(d) Explain the effect of an increase in the currency-to-deposit ratio on the money multiplier and the money supply. **(4 marks)**
(e) Suppose the central bank increases the monetary base to GHS 8,000. Recalculate the money supply using the multiplier from (b) and briefly comment on the implication for monetary policy. **(4 marks)**
answer:
**(a)** Money supply $M = C + D$; monetary base $B = C + R$ with reserves $R = (rr + e)D$. Let $c = C/D$. Then $M = (c + 1)D$ and $B = (c + rr + e)D$, so
$$m = \frac{M}{B} = \frac{1 + c}{c + rr + e}.$$
$c$ (currency-to-deposit ratio): how much cash the public holds relative to deposits; cash outside banks cannot be lent. $rr$ (required reserve ratio): share of deposits banks must hold by law. $e$ (excess reserve ratio): extra reserves banks choose to hold. Each is a **leakage** from the deposit-creation process.

**(b)** $m = \dfrac{1 + 0.2}{0.2 + 0.10 + 0.05} = \dfrac{1.2}{0.35} \approx$ **3.43**.

**(c)** $M = 3.43 \times 5{,}000 \approx$ **GHS 17,142.86**.

**(d)** A higher $c$ means more cash is held outside banks, so fewer reserves support deposit creation: the **multiplier falls** (the denominator rises by more than the numerator in proportion, since $rr + e < 1$) and the **money supply falls** for a given base.

**(e)** $M = 3.43 \times 8{,}000 \approx$ **GHS 27,428.57**. A GHS 3,000 increase in the base raises the money supply by about GHS 10,286: the central bank can expand money supply by more than the base injection, but the size of the effect depends on public and bank behaviour ($c$ and $e$), so control is imperfect.

> [!answer]
> $m = (1 + c)/(c + rr + e) = 1.2/0.35 \approx 3.43$; M ≈ GHS 17,142.86; higher c lowers m and M; with B = 8,000, M ≈ GHS 27,428.57.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The multiplier shows how the banking system multiplies base money through lending. It is endogenous: the public's cash preference and banks' excess reserves (which rise in uncertain times) can weaken monetary policy transmission.

## Simplified explanation

Every cedi of base money ends up as about 3.43 cedis of money in circulation. Holding more cash or reserves reduces this, because less is lent out.
hint: M = C + D, B = C + R.

options.text: composed only of checkable deposits.
Money that is in a commercial bank vault.
Money because the government asserts that it is.
Money that can be redeemed for a valuable commodity such as gold.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

**Fiat money** has no intrinsic value and is not redeemable for a commodity; it is money because the government declares it legal tender.

## Simplified explanation

It's money because the government says so.

body: Demand deposits are classified as money because:

options.text: They can be readily used in purchasing goods and paying debts.
options.hint: Correct. They serve as a medium of exchange.

options.text: Banks hold currency equal to the value of their checkable deposits.
They are ultimately the obligations of the Treasury.
They earn interest income for the depositor.
options.hint: Many earn none; not why they are money.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Demand deposits are money because cheques and transfers drawn on them are generally accepted for payments: they function as a medium of exchange.

## Simplified explanation

You can pay with them.

options.text: Investment but not to net exports or government spending.
Investment, net export and government spending.
options.hint: Correct. Any change in autonomous spending is multiplied.

options.text: Increases in spending but not to decreases in spending.
Spending by the private sector but not by the public sector.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A change in any component of autonomous aggregate expenditure (I, G, NX, autonomous C) changes equilibrium income by a multiple $1/(1 - MPC)$ in the simple model, in either direction.

## Simplified explanation

Any extra spending gets multiplied.

body: The MPC can be defined as that fraction of a:

options.text: Change in income that is not spent.
Change in income that is spent.
Given total income that is not consumed.
Given total income that is consumed

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$MPC = \Delta C/\Delta Y$: the share of an extra cedi of income spent on consumption.

## Simplified explanation

The part of extra income you spend.

body: What is the term for paper money that is not backed by gold or silver, but instead has a set limit of issuance determined by the central bank?

options.text: Near Money
options.hint: Near money is liquid assets like savings deposits.

options.text: Fiduciary Money
options.hint: Correct. Paper money issued beyond metal backing, on trust, within a fiduciary limit.

options.text: Liquidity
options.hint: A property, not a type of money.

options.text: Money Substitutes

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

**Fiduciary issue** is currency not backed by gold/silver, issued on trust up to a limit set by the monetary authority.

## Simplified explanation

Money issued on trust = fiduciary.

body: Which of the following components of money includes the sum of currency held by the public, demand deposits, other checkable deposits and traveler's checks?

options.text: M0
M1
options.hint: Correct. Currency + demand and checkable deposits + traveler's cheques.

options.text: M2
options.hint: M1 + savings and small time deposits.

options.text: Beyond M2

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

**M1** (narrow money) = currency in circulation + demand deposits + other checkable deposits + traveler's cheques: the most liquid means of payment.

## Simplified explanation

The spending-money measure is M1.

body: Which of the following correctly represents the chronological stages in the evolution of money?

options.text: Commodity Money → Barter System → Metallic Money → Paper Money → Electronic Money
Barter System → Commodity Money → Metallic Money → Paper Money → Credit Money → Electronic Money
Paper Money → Commodity Money → Barter System → Credit Money → Mobile Money
Barter System → Metallic Money → Commodity Money → Paper Money → Digital Currency

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Money evolved from **barter** → **commodity money** (cattle, salt, cowries) → **metallic money** (coins) → **paper money** → **credit (bank) money** → **electronic/digital money**.

## Simplified explanation

Swapping goods came first, electronic money last.

body: Why is the process of money creation by commercial banks limited?

options.text: Because banks must convert all deposits into gold
Because customer withdrawals reduce demand for loans
Because the central bank sets a required reserve ratio limiting the amount banks can lend
options.hint: Correct. Reserve requirements cap deposit expansion.

options.text: Because interest income is capped by the government

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Each round of lending must leave a fraction of deposits as reserves, so deposit creation is limited to $1/rr$ times reserves (further reduced by cash leakages and excess reserves).

## Simplified explanation

Banks must keep some money back, so they can't lend forever.

body: During the evolution of money, which type of money represented a transitional stage where currency had no intrinsic value but was still backed by a physical commodity like gold or silver?

options.text: Fiat Money
Cryptocurrency
Representative Money
options.hint: Correct. Paper claims redeemable in gold/silver.

options.text: Commodity Money

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

**Representative money** (e.g. gold certificates) had no value itself but could be exchanged for a fixed amount of a commodity; it bridged commodity money and fiat money.

## Simplified explanation

Paper that you could swap for gold.

body:
Given the following structural equations of a hypothetical economy:

$C = 140 + 0.45Y_d$, $I = 80$, $T = 100$, $G = 120$, $X = 130$ and $M = 125$.

(a) Determine the equilibrium level of national income (Y). **[2 marks]**
(b) Calculate the general and tax multipliers. Interpret your answers. **[2 marks]**
(c) What effect will a 20% cut in government expenditure have on equilibrium national income? (Hint: use the government multiplier.) **[2 marks]**
(d) Suppose that the government introduces a tax rate of 10% on households' income. (i) Write out the new tax function. **[1 mark]** (ii) In part (a), what will be the new level of national income? **[2 marks]**
(e) Calculate the values of private, government and national savings. **[2 marks]**
answer:
**(a)** $Y = C + I + G + X - M = 140 + 0.45(Y - 100) + 80 + 120 + 130 - 125 = 300 + 0.45Y \Rightarrow 0.55Y = 300 \Rightarrow Y^* \approx$ **545.45**.

**(b)** Expenditure (general) multiplier $= \dfrac{1}{1 - 0.45} \approx$ **1.82**: a 1-unit rise in autonomous spending raises Y by 1.82. Tax multiplier $= \dfrac{-0.45}{0.55} \approx$ **−0.82**: a 1-unit rise in lump-sum taxes lowers Y by 0.82.

**(c)** $\Delta G = -0.2 \times 120 = -24$; $\Delta Y = 1.82 \times (-24) \approx -43.64$, so Y falls to about **501.82**.

**(d)** (i) $T = 100 + 0.10Y$. (ii) $Y_d = 0.9Y - 100$; $C = 95 + 0.405Y$; $Y = 95 + 0.405Y + 205 \Rightarrow 0.595Y = 300 \Rightarrow Y \approx$ **504.20**.

**(e)** (At the equilibrium in (a).) $Y_d = 445.45$, $C = 140 + 0.45(445.45) = 340.45$. Private saving $= Y_d - C = $ **105**. Government saving $= T - G = 100 - 120 = $ **−20** (deficit). National saving $= 105 - 20 = $ **85** $= I + (X - M) = 80 + 5$ ✓.

> [!answer]
> Y ≈ 545.45; multipliers 1.82 and −0.82; 20% cut in G → Y ≈ 501.82; with T = 100 + 0.1Y, Y ≈ 504.20; private saving 105, public −20, national 85.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

In an open economy national saving equals investment plus net exports: $S + (T - G) = I + (X - M)$. A proportional income tax flattens the AE line (slope $0.45 \times 0.9 = 0.405$), lowering the multiplier from 1.82 to 1.68.

## Simplified explanation

Total spending must equal income: Y = 300 + 0.45Y gives about 545. Cutting government spending by 24 lowers income by about 44. Households save 105, the government dissaves 20.
